0.original: Alphinaud is eager to gather information on the heretics.

1.original: Alphinaud asks that you aid him in questioning the Convictors. Make your way around the camp, and learn what you can of the heretic presence in the area.

2.original: To your frustration, none of the Convictors seem to know anything about Lady Iceheart or her followers. Try questioning the soldier Pierriquet.

3.original: After fruitlessly interrogating dragonslayers of all descriptions, the lowborn soldier, Pierriquet, finally provides you with a valuable piece of information. According to him, heretics in the western highlands are summoned with purple-hued signal smoke. Perhaps your quarry can be made to come to you...

48.original: Surely one of these people will have encountered heretics while out hunting. Pray speak with as many as you can, <hex:022C0DFF07022903EB0203FF02200203>.

49.original: I've not seen Lady Iceheart myself, but we Convictors range far and wide in search of our prey. Mayhap one of my fellow dragonslayers has a helpful tale to tell.

50.original: While this is, I confess, a somewhat tedious business, one of these people may have valuable knowledge that will save us days of searching.

51.original: ...I may have erred in seeking the wisdom of these whelps.

52.original: Ah, 'tis colder than Lady Iceheart's frost-rimed...uh, soul! Greetings, <hex:020813E905FF076D696C616479FF076D696C6F726403>! A fine day, is it not?

53.original: Be still! How am I supposed to watch for the distant flicker of dragon wings when my ears are ringing with your incessant chatter!?

54.original: Nay, I know of no heretics. Do you honestly expect me to keep track of every Raitmeaux, Vairemont, and Bertennant that wanders in and out of camp?

55.original: Nay, I know of no heretics. Do you honestly expect me to keep track of every Raitmeaux, Vairemont, and Bertennant that wanders in and out of camp?

56.original: Hm? Are there any heretics in the area? I have not the faintest idea. Why, a heretic could pass under my very nose and I should be none the wiser.

57.original: I hunt <hex:021A020203>dragons<hex:021A020103>, my dear <hex:020811E905FF056C616479FF0766656C6C6F7703>! The big ones! Forever do I scan the skies for signs of my prey─I care not for the miserable creatures that scurry upon the ground!

58.original: Hm? Are there any heretics in the area? I have not the faintest idea. Why, a heretic could pass under my very nose and I should be none the wiser.

59.original: I hunt <hex:021A020203>dragons<hex:021A020103>, my dear <hex:020811E905FF056C616479FF0766656C6C6F7703>! The big ones! Forever do I scan the skies for signs of my prey─I care not for the miserable creatures that scurry upon the ground!

60.original: Looking for heretics, you say? Hmph. Why don't you go and bother Pierriquet or someone?

61.original: I've enough trouble keeping these preening fops fed and clothed as it is. 'Tis no business of mine what folk do with themselves out there in the wilds.

62.original: Looking for heretics, you say? Hmph. Why don't you go and bother Pierriquet or someone?

63.original: Summat I can help you with, <hex:020813E905FF076D696C616479FF076D696C6F726403>?

64.original: Heretics, is it? Well, I've never seen one meself...but that ain't to say I haven't heard a thing or two.

65.original: We would be grateful for any information you can share with us. The gods know we've gleaned precious little from talking to the rest of these...people.

66.original: If it please milord, I'm Pierriquet─a soldier by trade, though not much of one, if I'm honest. It weren't for the love of stabbing folk that I took up the spear, see.

67.original: No, it was by order of Ser Jantellot's father. Still, as long as they keep paying me wages, I ain't fussy as to what they have me do.

68.original: Not everyone's as patient as me, though. Plenty of lowborn lads who get pressed into service start grumbling before they've seen their second battle.

69.original: And once they've got to thinking how unfair it all is, it don't take much for the heretics to turn their heads. From what I hear, the simple promise of freedom tends to do it.

70.original: That may explain how Lady Iceheart was able to expand her following so swiftly.

71.original: Sad to say, some mates of mine gobbled down the heretics' tripe and asked for seconds─told me they were off to the western highlands to light a signal fire. That's how you let the heretics know you're serious about joining their ranks, apparently. Send up some purple smoke, and the bastards come to you.

72.original: ...Is that so? Why then...I am minded to start a fire.
